title: Fool Night
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A century of cloud cover has starved Earth of sunlight and oxygen, so people are paid to undergo 'transfloration', turning into oxygen-producing plants over two years. Impoverished Toshiro Kamiya, robbed of his savings by his sick mother, volunteers, gains the ability to hear plants, and starts working as a go-between for families and transfloration subjects.
life_message: It asks whether a society that buys the bodies of its poorest still values human life, and holds up compassion amid despair.

content.note: A serial-killer thread and a former soldier character (MU Serial Killer/s; Wikipedia characters); AniList Body Horror 71%.
Dying world, bodies turning into plants, tragedy (Wikipedia plot; AniList Eco-Horror 100%, Tragedy 79%).
Toshiro chooses transfloration after losing all hope, a paid form of ending one's human life (Wikipedia plot; AniList Suicide tag, MU Moral Dilemma).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Toshiro absorbs wrongs from his mother rather than retaliating (Wikipedia plot).

Order vs freedom.evidence: A state system manages bodies and oxygen; individuals bound by it (AniList Dystopian, Politics).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Toshiro's duty to his ill mother drives him even as she exploits him (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Class divides and officials like Yatsuka hold power over the poor (AniList Class Struggle; Wikipedia characters).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: A technological, secular society, with a cult on the margins (AniList Cult).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pure survival: oxygen, money and medicine (Wikipedia plot).

folkways.japan: Filial duty to a parent despite mistreatment and quiet self-sacrifice for the household reflect Japanese family norms, set against a dystopian state.

delivery.evidence: AniList blurb poses transfloration as an open ethical question; no review found (to verify).

delivery.note: The social critique is built into the premise and posed as questions rather than answers (to verify).

winners_losers: Sympathy goes to the poor who sell themselves to survive and to Toshiro's compassion for the transformed; the system that commodifies them is critiqued.
